entries.title: the dead-code text fallback reads a file once
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` on an index that holds no call reference no longer costs time quadratic in the functions of one file. It decided whether each function had a caller by splitting the function's whole file, joining the lines outside it and searching the result, once per function. On one generated Python file the tool took 3.38 s at 2,872 functions, 13.68 s at 5,655 and 53.42 s at 11,109; the same three now take 0.05 s, 0.12 s and 0.22 s. Each file is read, split and tokenised once, and the answers are unchanged. The fallback's peak memory is higher (34.1 MB against 10.0 MB on this repository's source). A repository whose index holds any call reference never took this path.

entries.title: the index CLI chooses the index identity, and an existing directory is a local target
entries.summary: `jcodemunch-mcp index <path> --identity-mode local|git` chooses how a local path is keyed in the index store; the CLI always ran in `config` mode before. An explicit mode on a GitHub target is refused before any network call. A directory that exists is now a local target however it is spelled (`proj/`, `proj/sub`, `~/proj`), where the CLI sent those spellings to the GitHub indexer. That moves one command with no option: `index owner/repo` or `index github.com/owner/repo`, run where a directory of that relative name exists, now indexes the directory. `https://github.com/owner/repo` forces the remote. Requested by @sKlat-beep (#1017).

entries.title: ASP.NET Web Forms is indexed, and a handler wired in markup is referenced
entries.summary: ASP.NET Web Forms markup (.aspx, .ascx, .master, .asax, .ashx, .asmx) is indexed as its own language, `aspx`, and ten XML-shaped .NET files (.csproj, .resx, .xaml and others) as `xml`. An event handler wired only in markup (OnClick="btnSave_Click") now reads as referenced, and pages, handlers and project files are roots, so the dead-code tools stop offering live Web Forms code for deletion. Contributed by @outoftheblue9. An existing C# index that holds one of the new file types over the size cap now reads as an inadequate corpus until `max_file_size` covers the file.

entries.title: the dynamic-import scan walks a Python file once
entries.summary: Indexing a Python file that holds a dynamic import walked the file's whole syntax tree once or twice per literal table, once per loop variable and once per pass, a cost added in 1.108.320. The file is now walked once. A cold index of this project's own source is about an eighth faster on Linux, and the edges the scan returns are unchanged, so no index needs rebuilding. About a tenth of a cold index against the code before 1.108.320 is not recovered.
